newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada oil industry pleased with election result.
newsitem.headline: Canada oil industry pleased with election result.

text.p: Canada's oil and gas industry reacted positively to standings after the Monday general election, which resulted in a reduced Liberal majority and a win for the country's energy minister.

"I think that the oilpatch is relieved that there is at least a majority government, particularly given that you've got a third of the House (of Commons) that could be identified as regional parties," David Manning, president of the Canadian Association of Petroleum Producers, said in an interview late Monday.
Manning said Canada's energy industry has always been perceived as western-based, often putting it at odds with the traditional eastern Canadian political power base.
But full-scale production of oil and gas is set to start in Newfoundland and Nova Scotia during the new term, which will serve to reduce the polarization which dates back decades, he said.
CAPP, which represents 190 producing companies, is the Canadian energy industry's main lobbying organization.
Canada's Liberals on Monday won a reduced majority government, with the western-based Reform Party unseating the separatist Bloc Quebecois as the country's official opposition.

Natural Resources Minister Anne McLellan, who regained her seat in Edmonton, was one of just a handful of Liberals to win in the western provinces, where the lion's share of Canadian oil and gas is currently produced.
"What ever role she plays in the next cabinet, her election is a very positive thing for the oilpatch," Manning said.
"She's one of the only voices from Alberta...More importantly, she's one of the few people in the caucus who really understands the issues facing the energy industry."
McLellan, who was an oil and gas novice when she became energy minister in 1993, played major roles in numerous initiatives lauded by Canada's energy industry.

Last year, she convinced the government to ease the tax burden for companies starting up capital-intensive oil sands mining and extraction projects, a move that has helped lead to billions of dollars in new spending.

She has also advocated voluntary measures for companies to curb greenhouse gas emissions, which has been welcomed by oil companies, but decried by environmentalists. ((Reuters Calgary Bureau (403) 531-1624))
